content.thinking:
I'm planning to write the whole file in one careful pass without testing, designing a qilin as a quadruped with a deer-like body, dragon head, antlers, scales, hooves, cloud mane, and ox tail, roughly 1.6m at the shoulder and 2m long, with antlers reaching about 2.3m, while keeping the design manageable.

Now I'm working out the skeleton structure: a root hips joint, spine chain running forward to the chest, a curving neck chain rising toward the head, and separate chains for the tail and limbs, using catmull paths to define smooth joint positions and orienting the head joint relative to the end of the neck chain.

For the head, I'm planning dragon-like features -- a skull, snout, and upper/lower jaw joints positioned relative to the head location. For the body mesh, I'm thinking through how to sweep a skinned surface along the spine path, extending it from the rump to the chest so it covers the whole torso rather than just the joint segment.

Now I'm working out radii at key points along the body (rump, belly, chest) and checking the belly height clears the ground, then sizing the hind legs with three segment lengths for a slender, digitigrade deer-like stance.

For the leg chain itself, I'm verifying hip-to-hoof distance fits within the segment sum, then deciding bend directions for the knee and hock joints, and figuring out naming for the four joint points (hip, knee, hock, fetlock) across the three limb spans.

Now I'm working out the front legs similarly: shoulder position, target near the ground, with segment lengths summing a bit longer than the straight-line distance to allow slight bending, using elbow-back and carpus-forward joint directions. I'm also noting that the legs should parent to the last spine joint.

I'm thinking through leg thickness tapers and picking a color palette for the qilin—pearl white body with jade teal scale patches on the back and flanks, leaning toward an elegant white-and-gold high-fantasy look.

Working out specifics: pale gold belly, cyan/white/gold gradient cloud-card mane, gold antlers, gold-bronze hooves, a flame/cloud tuft tail, and glowing eyes, forehead gem, and rune marks on the flanks. I'm building the cel-shaded coat paint with fur edges in jade and pale gold, subtle teal ink lines, then layering scale paint on top.

Defining scale colors and parameters...

Writing leg sock shading logic...

Now I'm working out the neck sweep, starting from the chest joint with a radius tapering from 0.2 down toward the head, keeping continuity with the body's end cap. Then I'm setting up the head joint at the end of the neck, beginning the skull as a scaled sphere part.

For the horse-dragon muzzle, I'm shaping the upper jaw as a tapering frustum running forward from the head joint, but considering a rounded sweep instead of a blocky box for a smoother profile.

Now setting up a separate jaw joint parented to the head for the lower jaw, with its own sweep geometry rigged to that bone, plus plans for teeth, fangs, and long dragon-style whiskers.

Adding nostrils, a goatee tuft under the jaw, and decal-based eyes placed on the sides of the skull with mirrored positioning and contrasting amber irises against the teal head.

I'll stick a small glowing teal gem on the forehead. For the antlers, I'm planning to sprout them from skull hits near the top-back, using a zero-count sprout so they ride directly on the head bone, with the main beam as a curved path and branches computed manually in model space rooted to the head joint.

Still plotting beam points... though I'm realizing the antler height might push the total silhouette too tall relative to the head, so I may need to scale back the curve's reach.

Now I'm sketching the tine branches off the main beam using a catmull path with tangent sampling, placing short offshoots at a few points along the curve to give it that natural antler forking look.

Placing rings along the path, I need to work out orientation since path points lack bone info, so I'll explicitly pass bone: head and use the frame's tangent direction to orient a thin disc shape correctly in the XY plane.

Moving on to the ears, I'm planning frill-like fins extruded from 2D outlines positioned on the back and cheeks of the head, sketching outline point coordinates and figuring out the extrude direction vector to orient them correctly.

For the mane texture down the neck and chest, I'm planning cloud-shaped curly tufts rendered as SVG swirl textures in teal/white/gold, placed along the neck's dorsal line using frame sampling. I need to work out the right call signature for generating frames along the neck sweep to attach these cards.

Planning three layered rows of cloud cards around the neck at varying angles, mixing teal-white, gold-cream, and jade textures for visual drama, plus extending the mane along the spine toward the withers using a partial sweep range.

Adding smaller cloud puffs at the leg joints — elbows and hocks — with a few rotating cards each for that qilin-tufted look, and shaping a curved, bushy tail with an upward catmull-rom arc out from the body.

Setting the tail tuft flow direction toward the tangent for a natural downward drape, and thinking about whether the mane cards should glow slightly. For the hooves I'm sketching cloven shapes using small frustum cylinders placed at each leg tip, sized to sit just above floor level.

Adding toe and dew claw details...

Placing decals...

Now I'm considering whether glowing the flank swirl decal is safe—glow requires a standard material, and since decals use textured meshes they should qualify, but I want to weigh the risk before applying it.

For ornamentation, I'm thinking a qilin wouldn't wear armor, so instead I'll add a gold-jade collar torus around the neck base, complete with a jade gem and tassels for a Genshin-style touch, and I'm working out the right joint and surface point to loop the sweep around.

Adding gold tassel cords hanging from the gem with beaded ends, then moving on to gold ring bracelets and anklets swept around the leg frames at key points along the chain.

Next I'm planning whiskers for the dragon muzzle, curling gold strands with teal tip bands, before sketching out the stylized horse-dragon hybrid head.

Adding more facial details now: a small pink tongue inside the jaw, brow ridge spikes angled back above the eyes, gold-edged cheek fins behind the jaw hinge with jade fill, glowing gold antler tines, and small leaf-shaped swept-back ears.

Working out the head's position relative to the neck and body — placing the skull center, sizing it with a scaled sphere, and extending the snout forward while keeping proportions consistent with the chest and body heights. Skipping belly ribbing and spine detail for now, focusing instead on the body paint using the coat color.

I'm deciding to skip extra dorsal spikes and scale studs to keep part count reasonable, prioritizing correctness over richness given I can't visually verify the result. Checking that hooves sit at floor level and other extremities like antlers, whiskers, and tail tuft clear the ground properly, then starting on a cloud-texture SVG generator function that draws a swirling flame-like pattern using the main, light, dark, and accent colors.

Writing SVG code...

Now I'm thinking through color variants for the cloud—planning a white-teal anime-style palette with distinct main, light, dark, and swirl accent colors for each version.

Writing SVG spiral code...

Now I'm moving to setting up the actual scene code, planning imports for the Three.js builder and frame utilities, though some may end up unused.

Trimming imports down to only what's needed—paths, rigging, paint, and toon shading kits—then starting the metadata export for the Qilin creature.

Setting up the builder with a 2048 paint size and seeded randomness, then defining the color palette: golds, ivory, a teal glow, dark ink, nose teal, tongue pink, and a coral accent.

Still defining coat paints...

Building spine chain and body sweep...

Still refining body proportions...

Now I'm setting up the neck chain, parented to the last spine joint, with a curve running up and forward from the chest toward the head position.

Then I'm defining the head joint attached to the neck's end, oriented downward and forward, and placing the skull center just beyond the neck tip so the neck's rounded cap tucks into it naturally.

Writing snout sweep points...

Then I'll add the nose pad as a scaled sphere positioned at the snout tip, plus two small dark nostril spheres offset left and right near the nose.

For the jaw, I'm setting up a joint parented to the head with an aim target toward the snout, then sketching a lower jaw sweep curve from the jaw joint through a mid-point to the tip.

Adjusting positions so the snout bottom and jaw top overlap slightly to read as a closed mouth, tweaking the down-offsets and radii until the gap closes properly. Now I'm thinking about adding a chin beard tuft using card elements bound to the jaw bone, positioned relative to the head's local frame.

Setting up three or four gold beard cards hanging downward with a cloud texture, attached to the jaw at increasing forward offsets, then moving on to add the upper fangs as spikes positioned near the mouth in ivory.

Now I'm placing lower fang teeth from the jaw base angled upward, skipping extra small teeth and the tongue since the mouth stays closed. For the eyes, I'm casting rays around the skull surface at mirrored left/right angles to find hit points, then placing eye decals sized appropriately at those spots, mirroring for the opposite side.

I'm working out the azimuth geometry so the eyes land correctly on the ellipsoid skull surface near the front-sides, accounting for the muzzle's forward offset. Then I'm adding gold brow spikes positioned above each eye, angled back and outward from a similar surface hit point.

Still defining whisker curve points...

Now I'm placing a forehead gem with a teal octahedron embedded and a gold cylindrical setting around its base, then starting to figure out the antler geometry branching from the skull's top anchor point.

I'm plotting the main antler beam as a catmull-rom curve through several head-local points, tapering its sweep radius from thick at the base to a pointed tip, and noting the head's downward tilt doesn't affect these local coordinates. Now I'm starting to define the tines branching off the beam at various points along its length.

Adding tine tip glow and ring details...

Now I'm designing the fin shape for the jaw hinge, sketching an outline that extends back and up with a sharp point before tapering down, checking it doesn't self-intersect.

I'm deciding on fin colors, going with a light jade/teal tone for the main fin, and planning a reusable function to place additional smaller gold fins at scaled positions around the head.

Now I'm working out leg placement, calculating hip and shoulder joint positions relative to the body's surface radius, then verifying the limb segment lengths roughly match the distance between hip and foot targets so the IK bends work out correctly.

I'm defining the leg chains with four joints each, swept with tapering radii from hip down to hoof, and checking that the chain's path includes the tip point for a smooth sweep. The front legs attach to the last spine joint as their parent.

Next I'm adding muscle spheres at the hip and shoulder joints for thigh and shoulder bulges, positioning them to slightly protrude beyond the body silhouette for a natural muscular look, then working out how to reference each leg's terminal tip joint for placing the hooves.

Now I'm building the hoof toes as small cylinders attached to the tip joint, checking that their geometry overlaps cleanly with the leg's rounded cap so there's no visible gap, and adding a gold band cylinder around the hoof as decorative trim.

I'm keeping the color palette limited to around 20 flat tones, skipping dewclaws, and sketching an anklet by sweeping a chain loop around the leg surface at a point along the cannon between the hock and the hoof tip.

For the leg cloud puffs, I'm placing outward-facing tufted cards at the elbow and hock points, choosing angles to the sides, sizing them small with moderate lean and bend, and positioning them roughly around the hock and knee along the leg sweep so the cards stand outward from the surface normal.

Now sketching the tail as a tapering curve from rump to tip with shrinking radius, plus a tuft of hair cards clustered near the end.

Adding dorsal frame cards...

For the neck mane, I'm building rows of frames at different angles along the neck tube, looping through angle positions and time steps to place cards with sizes that taper down for off-center rows versus the central ridge row.

I'm also considering adding a chest plume row near the neck base at the underside angles, but worrying those frames will face downward and render dark since normal-based shading won't be lit there — deciding to skip tinting fixes and maybe narrow the angle range instead of fully fixing the shading issue.

For the collar, I'm surfacing just the neck tube and placing a gold swept loop around it near the base, being careful the plane doesn't also cut through the body mesh. Since the mane cards cluster around certain angles, I'm thinking of shifting the collar slightly further down the neck so it stays visible beneath the mane.

For the pendant, I'm locating a front-facing point on the neck tube using the sweep frame, then attaching a gem with a gold cylindrical setting, plus a few short dangling rods as tassels hanging below it.

Still figuring out how the tassel rods should be bone-weighted — since they're built from raw points rather than proper sweep anchors, I need to explicitly assign them to the nearest neck joint instead of relying on automatic weighting.

Now I'm planning flank and thigh swirl decals on the body surface, positioning them with appropriate offsets and sizing. I'm weighing whether to add a glow effect, worried that the decal's material might not be compatible since glow logic sometimes checks for a "paint" material name—since this texture is applied rather than painted, I'll risk applying a modest glow anyway.

Skipping extra bell and jewel accents. Checking that the neck cap sleeve fits properly into the skull socket and that antler height stays around 2.3 total, then roughly tallying up part counts across body, neck, head, antlers, and legs to gauge scene complexity.

Total part count comes out around 150 once legs, tail, and card decals are included, which seems reasonable, and the color palette list looks sufficient. Now I'm writing a helper function to generate cloud shapes using layered bump coordinates for a soft puffy outline.

Generating SVG cloud layers...

I'm realizing a key problem: if mane cards are flat standing planes facing front/back, they'd be edge-on and invisible from the side profile view, so I need to use crossed card geometry to keep the mane visible from multiple angles.

I'm setting up the cloud sheets lying along the neck angle and wiring up the texture arrays and frame types for the cards, plus planning a crest tuft of cards between the horns on top of the head.

For the chin and head-top hits, I'm sampling the skull surface at a few angles, filtering out null results since the hit could miss. I'm guarding the brow hit lookups similarly, and confirming that a Hit automatically sets its direction from the surface normal so the eye decals can just reference the hit point directly. Now I'm adding metadata fields like name, description, style, and commit before moving on to a helper for the horn/head geometry.

I'm writing a helper function that converts side, length, up, and forward offsets into a local coordinate object, handling negative forward values by swapping to a "back" key and negative side values by swapping to "right" instead of "left" since the local() method likely only accepts positive directional keys.

Sketching the leg paint function to distinguish sock and coat coloring based on a zigzag pattern, then setting up the glow effect on the gem stick and the tail tuft ring using the chain's endpoint.

I'm also working out how to collect dorsal frame points along the body sweep between t=0.35 and 0.95, pushing each sampled point into a typed array for later use.

Now I'm building the leg geometry, looping over left/right sides and computing hip and foot positions for the hind limbs using the limb helper with bend lengths.

Structuring a leg function that builds the joint chain with proper naming conventions per side and tag, importing the Joint type from the skeleton module to wire up parent joints and radii for each segment.

Adding a gold anklet band at the cannon and setting leg radii arrays for hind and front legs, then skipping the belly band idea and finalizing by returning the root with descriptive text.
